text: This is Envoy, your private AI agent to the cloud. Your device keeps the secrets. The cloud does the thinking.
Every day, people paste leases, offer letters, lab results and secret keys into cloud AI. Today, all of it leaves the device, and you can't take it back.
Envoy changes the deal. The private steps run on Chrome's built-in model, right on your device, and the cloud only ever sees tags.
As you type, Envoy finds what is private, and turns names, emails, phone numbers and amounts into tags that keep their meaning.
It works for anyone. An HR manager checking an offer letter. A patient with lab results. A developer pasting a config with live keys. Each gets help, without handing over the details.
Here is a real session in private mode, on Gemma four, the model Gemini Nano four is built on. Mona asks whether her landlord can raise her rent by twenty percent.
Chrome's built-in model works through her lease on this laptop. The privacy flight recorder shows every step, where it ran, which model, and how long it took.
Before anything leaves, Mona sees exactly what the cloud will see. Only the clauses her question needs, with every name and number already a tag. Nothing is sent until she approves.
If a raw detail slips back in, like a bank account number pasted into the excerpt, the guard blocks the send.
Gemini four Hydrogen reasons over the tags, and writes the maths as an expression. Envoy works out the real amounts on her device, and puts Mona's details back.
Some questions never need the cloud. When does my lease end? Gemma four answers on the device, and zero bytes leave the laptop.
The network ledger lists every request, and exactly what reached the cloud.
This is hybrid inference with Firebase AI Logic. Finding, trimming, routing and local answers run only on the device, with a guard that checks they really did. Only the reasoning goes to the cloud.
The Chrome extension brings Envoy to any AI chat. A plain bank account number lights up as you type, and one click swaps every detail for a tag.
Upload with Envoy rebuilds files on your device. Photos lose their location data, and you can black out an ID number before it goes.
No on-device model yet? Envoy checks this computer and walks you through turning on private mode. Until then, Basic protection masks the details with local rules.
We measured it. On thirty six documents, private mode on Gemma four found every planted detail, leaked none, and sent about sixteen percent of the text. The guard stopped all twenty eight attacks.
Envoy. Ask the cloud. Keep your secrets.
